title: Beyond the 956: 'Cowboy' Bill Watts, WWE Hall of Famer and Mid-South promoter, dies at 87
excerpt: "Cowboy" Bill Watts, the WWE Hall of Famer who built Mid-South Wrestling into one of the most influential territories in professional wrestling, died November 17, 2026, at 87. His son Erik shared the news, and WWE confirmed his death; no cause of death was disclosed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

"Cowboy" Bill Watts, the WWE Hall of Famer who built Mid-South Wrestling into one of the most influential territories in professional wrestling history, has died at 87.

Watts died November 17, 2026. The news was announced Tuesday by veteran wrestling journalist Bill Apter, who shared a message from Watts' son Erik: "Dear Bill, my father, Cowboy Bill Watts, passed away today." WWE confirmed his death, saying, "WWE is saddened to learn that WWE Hall of Famer 'Cowboy' Bill Watts has passed away." No cause of death was disclosed.

Born William F. Watts Jr. on May 5, 1939, in Oklahoma City, Watts began his wrestling career in 1962 and became a star heavyweight across the United States and Japan. He made his greatest mark behind the scenes: from 1979 to 1987 he ran Mid-South Wrestling out of Shreveport, Louisiana, later renamed the Universal Wrestling Federation, where he pioneered episodic, storyline-driven weekly wrestling television. The territory launched and showcased future stars including Junkyard Dog, Ted DiBiase, "Hacksaw" Jim Duggan, Sting and the Ultimate Warrior.

Watts later served as Executive Vice President of WCW in 1992 and briefly worked as a booker for the WWF in 1995. He was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2009, the Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame and the George Tragos/Lou Thesz Hall of Fame in 2013, and was part of the inaugural class of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter Hall of Fame in 1996.

Watts is remembered as one of the most influential promoters and bookers in the history of professional wrestling, whose way of presenting the sport on television shaped the industry for decades.

Sources: WWE; Sports Illustrated; F4WOnline/Wrestling Observer; Wrestling Inc.
